quote: sorting stocks on the difference between historical realized volatility and at-the-money implied volatility. We find that a zero-cost trading strategy that is long (short)
title: Goyal & Saretto, Cross-section of option returns and volatility (abstract)

claim: Carr & Wu (RFS 2009) measure the VRP as realized variance minus a synthetic variance swap rate, for five stock indexes and 35 individual stocks (abstract only; sign/magnitude not in abstract, full PDF could not be read).
quote: investigate the historical behavior of variance risk premiums on five stock indexes and 35 individual stocks
title: Carr & Wu, Variance Risk Premiums (abstract)

claim: Cao & Han (JFE 2013): delta-hedged equity option returns fall monotonically with the underlying's idiosyncratic volatility; controlling for limits-to-arbitrage proxies cuts the effect by about 40%. Implication: options on high-idio-vol stocks are expensive, so long positions there do worse.
quote: delta-hedged equity option return decreases monotonically with an increase in the idiosyncratic volatility of the underlying stock.
title: Cao & Han, Cross section of option returns and idiosyncratic stock volatility (abstract)

claim: Cao & Han sample Jan 1996-Oct 2009 (~200K obs): delta-hedged calls lose on average 4.89% of option price from 1.5 months before expiry to expiry (secondary summary; indicates average negative return to long delta-hedged options).
quote: delta-hedged call options lose on average 4.89% (0.48%) of the option (underlying stock) price from 1.5 months before expiration to expiration.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Cao & Han

claim: Cao & Han low-minus-high idio-vol delta-hedged ATM call strategy earns about 2% per month at mid quotes, but adding friction of 50-100% of the bid-ask spread reduces it from about 1% per month to approximately zero (secondary summary).
quote: Adding trading friction equal to 50%, 75% or 100% of the closing option bid-ask spread incrementally reduces average profitability from about 1% per month to approximately zero.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Cao & Han

claim: Cao & Han effect decreases with market cap of the underlying (larger stocks, smaller effect) (secondary summary).
quote: The average return decreases systematically with the market capitalization of the underlying stock.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Cao & Han
